why: Replacing C8 introduced explicit checks that penalize isolating tiny right‑hand completions and that try to catch noun‑head/apposition separations; this slightly helped very short piece decisions (≤3 words) but shifted top scoring cuts in mid/long bins so the model often cut earlier inside clauses (splitting verbs from adverbs and detaching appositives), lowering H_set overall.
lesson: When adding semantic checks, avoid asymmetric penalties that protect tiny right fragments at the cost of creating incentives to split heads from their modifiers or appositives—apply the checks so they do not encourage earlier, intra‑clausal cuts.
